subject: biology-1
question: The **octet rule** says atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons so that their outermost **electron shell** holds eight electrons. Oxygen has six valence electrons. Which statement correctly applies the octet rule to oxygen?

options.text: Oxygen will lose six electrons to empty its outer shell.
Oxygen will gain six electrons to fill its outer shell.
Oxygen will gain two electrons to complete its outer shell.
Oxygen will gain two neutrons to stabilize its nucleus.

explanation: With six valence electrons, oxygen needs two more to reach the stable octet of eight, whether by gaining electrons or by sharing them in bonds. A would require an impossible transfer of six electrons. B ignores that the second shell can hold only eight electrons. D confuses electron configuration with nuclear stability.
